text:
Radek Faksa's second stint in Dallas looks a lot like his first: the Stars win his minutes, and he doesn't score. He has no goals and 2 assists in 15 games, on about 11 and a half minutes a night, and he's played over 14 minutes in each of the last two, both against Winnipeg and Buffalo.

No goals from 1.57 expected goals (the quality of his chances) is mostly bad luck, and goals were never the job anyway; and our range has him somewhere between 3 and 10 goals by season's end. What matters more is what happens at the other net. With Faksa on the ice at five on five, Dallas has had 55.1% of the expected goals, 4 points better than without him. That fits what Evolving-Hockey found last season: opponents got fewer good chances with him out there (92nd percentile among forwards), while his own offense was near the bottom of the league (bottom 4%). He's a 32-year-old checking center, drafted 13th overall by Dallas in 2012, and on a team with these ambitions that role still has a home.
headline: Faksa is back in Dallas, doing the quiet work
